title: Threat Modeling for Financial Ledger Microservices
business: FinTech organizations managing multi-tenant ledger systems.
problem: Unintended lateral movement between tenant data partitions due to poorly defined trust boundaries in microservice communication.
solution: Implementing a structured threat modeling process to map assets, identify trust boundaries, and define abuse cases, ensuring that every service-to-service request is explicitly mediated.
steps: Decompose the system architecture into distinct components and identify sensitive data assets.
Define trust boundaries between microservices and external ingress points to isolate tenant data.
Perform an adversary analysis to document potential abuse cases, such as unauthorized cross-tenant data access.
Design and implement specific mitigations, such as mutual TLS and granular authorization checks, for each identified threat.
Validate the effectiveness of mitigations against the documented abuse cases.
outcome: A hardened architecture where trust boundaries are explicitly enforced, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized cross-tenant data exposure.
limitation: Threat modeling is a point-in-time exercise; architectural drift can invalidate assumptions, requiring periodic reviews to ensure security controls remain aligned with the current system state.
